bullets.title: NVDA: Blowout Q2 + 70% FY28 Revenue Guide; Street Nearly Unanimous Buy
bullets.body: NVDA reported Q2 revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY, beat by ~$4B) and EPS $2.22 vs $2.09 consensus; Data Center hit record $89B (+117% YoY). FY28 revenue guided at ~70% YoY growth (vs ~45% consensus), explicitly supply-constrained — management says unconstrained demand would support ~100%. Gross margins reset lower to 72-73% in FY28 (from 75%) on HBM cost inflation, bottoming at 71-72% in Jan-Q; price hikes on Vera Rubin/systems offset partially. Vera Rubin ramping fastest in company history (~20% of Oct-Q DC revenue). AWS partnership expanded to 2M additional GPUs through Q2 FY29. NVDA also acquiring Hugging Face for $12.9B. Supply commitments surged to $279B from $119B QoQ. Street consensus: 96% Buy, avg PT ~$325; JPM raised to $320, Citi to $315, UBS to $300, MS to $300, Jefferies Buy at $300, Wolfe OP at $275, KeyBanc OW at $330.

bullets.title: NVDA: NVHBM Custom Memory + Hugging Face Acquisition Add Strategic Depth
bullets.body: NVDA unveiled NVHBM, a custom HBM integrating the memory controller into the 3D stack rather than the XPU, delivering 30% more bandwidth, 15% lower power, and 25% more compute die area vs. standard HBM4E. Separately, NVDA agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B, securing the open-source AI model ecosystem; Microsoft had also held talks but those ended. NVDA also launched a revenue-sharing financing platform with $500B+ in third-party capital commitments.

bullets.title: MRVL: AI Custom ASIC Business Doubling to $4B in FY28; Earnings Due Tonight
bullets.body: MRVL reports after close tonight. JPM and OpCo model MRVL's custom ASIC business doubling to $4B+ in FY28, with the GOOGL partnership now estimated at $20B p.a. vs. prior buyside expectations of ~$12B. Networking opportunity seen as ~two-thirds of AI exposure. JPM raises PT to $145. Street estimates viewed as floor; path to $11-12 EPS power by CY28. MRVL trades 35x F28 EPS vs. AVGO/NVDA in the teens — key debate is confidence in longer-term datacenter upside.

bullets.title: CRM: Beat/Raise on cRPO and Agentforce; Claudeforce Deepens Anthropic Partnership
bullets.body: CRM reported Q2 revenue $11.35B (+11% YoY, beat); cRPO +14% CC vs. 13% guidance; FY27 revenue raised to $46.1-46.4B. Agentforce ARR reached $1.5B (+240% YoY); NNAOV strongest in four years; attrition near record lows. Salesforce and Anthropic launched Claudeforce (open beta September). FY27 raise includes ~$200M from Contentful/Fin acquisitions. Mizuho, JPM, Wolfe, DA Davidson all raised PTs ($260-$271). Bears note most FY27 organic raise was modest; MuleSoft/Tableau weak.

bullets.title: CRWD: 'Mythos Moment' Drives Record NNARR +51% YoY; ARR Guide Raised Sharply
bullets.body: CRWD Q2 net new ARR $333M (+51% YoY), far above $285M consensus — described as possible highest NNARR beat ever. Total ARR $5.84B (+25% YoY), fourth consecutive acceleration. AIDR ARR ~$30M, up from ~$3M two quarters ago (3x QoQ). FY27 ARR guide raised to $6.608B (implying $1.355B NNARR, +34% YoY). Management calls Mythos-driven demand 'durable.' Citi raises PT to $260, Mizuho to $250, Roth Buy at $230, DA Davidson Buy at $245, KeyBanc raises to $245, Wolfe raises to $230.

bullets.title: OKTA: cRPO Accelerates to +14% YoY; AI Agent Deals Emerging; Upgraded by BofA
bullets.body: OKTA Q2 revenue $805M (+11% YoY, beat); cRPO $2.585B (+14% YoY, 3pts above guidance); large enterprise wins ($1M+ ACV) +22% YoY; new products ~30% of bookings. OKta for AI Agents generating 'dozens' of >$1M deals. FY27 revenue guide raised to $3.216-3.226B; FCF margin guidance 28-29%. BofA upgraded to Neutral from Underperform, PT $170. Citi raises PT to $165 (Neutral), Mizuho raises PT, Roth Buy at $155, Wolfe raises PT to $190 (Outperform), KeyBanc raises PT to $190. Stock +20% post-earnings.

bullets.title: META: $18B Teen Settlement Removes Overhang; AI Product Roadmap Ahead of Connect
bullets.body: META settled multi-state teen safety lawsuit for up to $18B over 10 years; $10B legal charge accrued in Q3. Teens (<1% of revenue) subject to 2-hour daily limits on FB/IG. Settlement removes significant regulatory overhang. Watermelon AI agent platform launch targeted October 2026. Meta Connect Sept 23 as next catalyst. GS upgraded with bullish AI monetization view; Citi reiterates Buy at $800 PT. Hedgeye signals shifted META to bearish trend.

bullets.title: AVGO: Custom AI ASIC Revenue Set to Double Again; Trades at 18x CY27 vs. Peers at 31x
bullets.body: OpCo highlights AVGO as the #1 custom AI ASIC design house (Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI as customers). AI semiconductor revenue modeled +51% QoQ in F3Q, +215% YoY, and +250% YoY in F4Q. AVGO supply secured through 2028 with TSMC relationship on par with NVDA and Apple. Trades at 18x CY27E vs. AI peers at 31x. ARK Invest purchased 57,705 AVGO shares. Earnings due Sept 3 AH ($3.22 EPS est., $29.24B revenue).

bullets.title: INTC: 18A Yields Ahead of Targets; EMIB Packaging Confirmed as TSMC Rival
bullets.body: At the Deutsche Bank conference, Intel management was upbeat on foundry progress with 18A yields tracking ahead of targets. Separately, Intel's EMIB advanced packaging is confirmed as a rival to TSMC CoWoS, with strong yields and satisfied Google and MediaTek customers cited. Intel CFO expressed conviction on external customer relationships. INTC +2.37% on NVDA earnings halo.

bullets.title: PI (Pure Storage): FY27 Guide Raised 38% on Second Hyperscaler Win; JPM Raises PT to $145
bullets.body: PI reported Q2 revenue $1.186B (beat), EPS $0.70 vs. $0.58 consensus, operating profit +77% YoY. FY27 revenue guide raised to $5.03-5.07B (vs. $4.49B consensus), implying 37-38% growth. Company secured a second hyperscaler win expected to drive 'multiples of revenues' in FY28. JPM raises PT to $145 (33x FY28E EPS); Citi raises PT to $130, BofA upgrades to Buy at $150 PT. Core enterprise market characterized as entering 'breakout territory.'

bullets.title: SNPS: F3Q Beat-and-Raise; EDA Reaccelerating; Sept 30 Investor Day Key Catalyst
bullets.body: SNPS Q3 revenue $2.477B (+42% YoY), EPS $3.91 vs. $3.67 consensus; FY26 revenue raised ~$50M, EPS raised to $15.07, FCF raised $600M. Core EDA growth reaccelerating to double-digit in F4Q. IP growth 25-30% YoY. 30+ active Agentic AI customer engagements. Ansys synergies layering faster than expected. Baird upgraded to Outperform; Citi Buy at $610 PT; Wolfe OP at $575 PT; Mizuho OP at $550 PT. Sept 30 Investor Day seen as major catalyst for higher long-term targets and AI monetization clarity.

bullets.title: FSLR: BMO Upgrades to Outperform; Post-S232 Tariff Selloff Seen as Overdone
bullets.body: BMO Capital Markets upgraded FSLR from Market Perform to Outperform, raising PT to $263 from $237 (28% upside). Analyst Ameet Thakkar argues the post-Section 232 tariff selloff is overdone and sees a favorable window for 2029+ bookings. Competitive risks from Tesla viewed as more than priced in. FSLR +4.3% pre-market.

bullets.title: WSM: Strong 2Q Beat on AI Shopping and B2B; UBS Raises PT to $247
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma Q2 comps +6.2% (vs. +4.8% in Q1), all banners positive; B2B +14.5% including 20% contract growth; AI shopping assistant (Olive) associated revenue +620% YTD. FY26 comp guidance raised to +4-6.5% (from +2-6%). UBS raises PT to $247 (~21x CY28 EPS), maintains Neutral citing demanding valuation requiring several more quarters of execution. GS AM also flags WSM in morning note.

bullets.title: MU: Bullish on Memory; DRAM Prices Surging to 5-Year Highs on AI Demand
bullets.body: Multiple sources highlight structural AI-driven memory demand, with DRAM prices at 5-year highs — 1kg of South Korean DRAM now equivalent to 620 grams of gold (up from 120g in 2023 trough). NVDA's FY28 guidance locks in major HBM demand; memory supply seen under-supplied until Q2'28 (UBS). MU bullish thesis for 2026-2027 cited by multiple sources on structural demand and operating leverage. Memory chip buyers reportedly panic-hoarding inventory anticipating 2027 shortages.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE/AAOI: Optical Demand 'Extraordinary'; Supply Shortage Seen 12-18+ Months
bullets.body: At Jefferies Global Semis Conference, COHR described optical demand as 'extraordinary' with supply shortages expected for 12-18+ months; capacity expansion may need to exceed 4x current plan. CPO adoption pushed to 2H C28+, creating near-term NPO architecture opening. 1.6T transceiver shipments tracking toward 100M units in C27. NVDA's Spectrum-X Ethernet ecosystem partners include COHR (ELS) and LITE (high-power laser, optical alignment). Optics cycle bust risk questioned but current fundamentals cited as much stronger than late-1990s.

bullets.title: MRVL Pre-Earnings: Photonic Fabric + OMIB Technology Highlighted; Google Partnership Implies $20B pa
bullets.body: Ahead of tonight's MRVL earnings, multiple analysts flag the company's Photonic Fabric acquisition and forthcoming Optical Multi-Chip Interconnect Bridge (OMIB) as key technology catalysts. JPM models MRVL's Google partnership at $20B p.a. (vs. buyside expectations of ~$12B in FY27); custom ASIC business seen doubling to $4B+ in F28. Options imply 8.8% move. EPS consensus $0.93, revenue $2.72B.

bullets.title: OKTA/CRWD: Piper Sandler Bullish on Agentic Security Inflection; SEI Under Political Pressure
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's morning call: CRWD justified at ~30x CY27 revenue given NNARR +51% (strongest since 2021) and agentic threat monetization. OKTA Neutral at 8x CY27 revenue; AI revenue immaterial in F27 but meaningful in F28+. SEI (not in main universe) down 21% since 8/17 amid AI datacenter moratoriums in TX, PA, MI ahead of midterms — political pressure on power services group is a read-through risk for data center power names.

bullets.title: DELL/MDB/AVGO/HPE/CIEN: Key Upcoming Earnings Calendar
bullets.body: DELL reports Tue 9/2 AH ($4.91 EPS est., $44.93B revenue); MDB reports Tue 9/2 AH ($1.62 EPS est., $735M revenue, Atlas needs to accelerate to +30% YoY); AVGO reports Wed 9/3 AH ($3.22 EPS est., $29.24B); HPE reports Wed 9/3 AH ($0.93 EPS est., $11.95B); CIEN reports Thu 9/4 BM ($1.72 EPS est., $1.63B). MDB: JPM warns Atlas guide needs +1 point acceleration to +27% YoY to satisfy bulls.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Tariff Risk: White House Weighing Sweeping Chip Tariffs
bullets.body: Politico reports the Trump administration is considering new sweeping tariffs on semiconductors and goods made with semiconductors, with potential phase-in and relief for companies investing in US chip manufacturing. Multiple sources note this as a near-term risk but offset by relief mechanisms. Separately, Politico reports a tariff on South Korea is being considered over Coupang treatment. Potential read-through: negative for fabless names importing ASICs and positive for US fabs (INTC foundry).

bullets.title: T/VZ: FWA Availability Declining in July; Mixed Read for 3Q Net Add Acceleration
bullets.body: Wolfe FWA update: T-Mobile availability fell -5.0% MoM in July, AT&T -0.6%, Verizon -0.5%. AT&T's New York availability declined notably despite re-entry into the market in June. Broad availability decline contrasts with expectations for modest sequential net add acceleration at Verizon and AT&T in 3Q26. Relationship between availability decline and subscriber growth not yet visible.
